title: API reference
content:
#

All recording, configuration, and capture operations must run on Unity's main
thread.


Record an event#



C# caller attributes supply the calling file, member, and line automatically.
The default category is the part of eventName before its first .; names without
a separator use General.

Add recording points to game code or event-bus adapters explicitly; the package
does not intercept every C# event. Pass the returned session-aware TraceId as
parentId to asynchronous and coroutine follow-up work. Causality is not inferred
from timestamps.

Recording works in the Editor and Development Builds. Regular release builds
return an invalid TraceId. Since method arguments are evaluated before Record is
called, guard expensive DTO creation with if (EventTrace.IsEnabled).


EventTrace methods#

API                                       BEHAVIOR
EventTrace.Configure(options)             Validates and copies settings; resizing retains the newest
                                          records
EventTrace.StartSession(name, metadata)   Creates a session ID, snapshots metadata, and clears the
                                          buffer
EventTrace.Record(...)                    Stores a payload snapshot, caller location, explicit parent
                                          ID, and optional call stack
EventTrace.GetSnapshot()                  Returns the current immutable records in a new array
EventTrace.Capture()                      Returns a detached capture of the session, records, and
                                          dropped count
EventTrace.Clear()                        Clears the buffer without resetting the session ID or
                                          sequence counter
TraceCapture.ToJson()                     Exports format version 1 JSON
TraceCapture.FromJson(json)               Validates format, IDs, sequence, and parent links, then
                                          returns a detached capture

TraceRecord exposes read-only properties. GetSnapshot() returns records in
buffer order. Source objects are held through weak references; destroyed objects
and imported captures cannot be selected. Runtime object IDs are not persistent
identifiers across sessions.


Configuration and capture limits#

SETTING                   DEFAULT           ALLOWED VALUES
enabled                   true              Enable or disable recording
captureCaller             true              Capture caller file/member/line
captureStackTrace         false             Capture recording-time call stacks
maxEvents                 10000             1–100,000
maxPayloadCharacters      4096              128–65,536
maxStackTraceCharacters   8192              128–65,536
maxBufferCharacters       4 * 1024 * 1024   At least one maximum-sized payload, up to 64M characters

The buffer evicts the oldest records when either the event-count or character
budget is exceeded. DroppedCount includes records discarded by either limit. The
character budget limits managed string lengths, not exact process memory; record
objects, arrays, rendering, stack formatting, and JSON export need additional
memory.

Payload snapshots copy public fields and readable public properties, with a
default depth limit of 4 and at most 32 collection or object entries. Unity
objects store only name, ID, and type. Oversized payloads use valid JSON:
{"$truncated":true}. Cycles become <cycle>, excessive depth becomes <max-depth>,
and unreadable properties become <unreadable: ...>. Getter execution time is not
bounded, so use small data objects.

If a parent is evicted or belongs to another session, the UI indicates this
rather than linking to an unrelated event with the same sequence number.


Call stacks#

Caller location and call stack capture are independent. Caller location is
enabled by default and stores one file/member/line. Stack capture is disabled by
default.



The stack is captured inside Record, before payload getters are evaluated, and
omits the recorder's own frame. It represents the synchronous managed call chain
at that moment. File names and line numbers are included when debug symbols are
available; optimized or IL2CPP builds can provide less detail. Async and
coroutine continuations do not recreate earlier execution stacks.

maxStackTraceCharacters defaults to 8,192 and accepts 128–65,536. Longer stacks
are truncated. Stored stack characters count toward maxBufferCharacters; a
record larger than the entire buffer budget is dropped. The limit bounds
retained stack text, not the temporary allocation used to build the string.


Import and export#



JSON contains session ID, name, start UTC, metadata, event and parent IDs,
elapsed time and frame, category and severity, payload, source name and object
ID, caller location, and optional stack trace. Unity object references are not
exported. The optional stack field preserves format version 1 compatibility with
older files.

The Editor uses .etr by default. TraceCaptureImporter imports files in Assets as
TraceCaptureAsset objects. Its inspector displays a summary and preview and can
open the full capture in the browser. Runtime ToJson and FromJson methods do not
depend on the file extension.

Imports accept at most 16M characters and 100,000 records. The browser also
checks a 16MB file-size limit before reading. Large exports may exceed these
limits, so reduce capture limits or split captures.


Tests#

To run the package's EditMode tests in a consuming project, install Unity Test
Framework and add "testables": ["com.achive.event-tracer"] to
Packages/manifest.json. The runtime package does not depend on Test Framework or
Play Bookmarks.

title: Using the browser
content:
#

Enter Play mode and select an event in the Event Tracer window. Its details show
the recorded data, cause, effects, source object, and calling code. Search event
names and payloads, or narrow the list with category, severity, and source
filters.

The UI defaults to English. Use the language menu to switch to 한국어; the choice
is remembered.


Browser controls#

CONTROL                  USE IT TO
Record                   Turn event recording on or off
Pause view               Keep the displayed events still while recording continues
New session              Start a fresh session and empty the event list
Clear                    Empty the list while staying in the same session
Back to live             Return from an imported capture or paused view
Capture limits → Apply   Set recording limits and enable caller or stack capture


Call stacks#

Stack capture is off by default because it adds overhead. Enable Capture limits
→ Capture stack trace, click Apply, and reproduce the action. Select a newly
recorded event to read or copy its CALL STACK.

File names and line numbers depend on available debug symbols. Async work and
coroutines do not preserve an earlier synchronous call stack; pass parentId to
keep their cause-and-effect link.


Save and reopen a session#

Click Export to save the displayed session as an .etr file, including event
data, relationships, and recorded call stacks. Export captures you want to keep
before starting a new session.

Click Import to reopen a capture without changing live recording. You can also
select an .etr file in the Project window and choose Open in Event Tracer. Use
Back to live to return to the current session.


Troubleshooting#

 * No events? Check Record, clear search and filters, and confirm the game calls
   EventTrace.Record. Recording runs in the Editor or a Development Build.
 * No call stack? Enable stack capture, click Apply, and reproduce the action
   again. Existing events keep the information recorded at the time.
 * Missing older events or parents? The buffer removes old events when its
   limits are reached. Increase the limits under Capture limits or export
   shorter sessions.
 * Cannot select the source object? Supply source when recording. Selection is
   available while the object is alive; saved captures keep its name rather than
   a live reference.

title: Installation
content:
#

Event Tracer requires Unity 2022.3 or later. Recording works in the Editor and
Development Builds.


Install with OpenUPM#

With the OpenUPM CLI installed, run this from your Unity project folder:



To install through the Unity Editor:

 1. Open Edit → Project Settings → Package Manager and add a scoped registry:
    
    FIELD   VALUE
    Name    OpenUPM
    URL     https://package.openupm.com
    Scope   com.achive.event-tracer

 2. Click Apply, then open Window → Package Manager.

 3. Choose + → Add package by name, enter com.achive.event-tracer, and click
    Add.

See the OpenUPM installation guide for more help.


Install from a Git URL#

In Package Manager, choose + → Add package from git URL and enter:




Open Event Tracer#

Open Tools → Achieve → Event Tracer in the Unity Editor. Start a session for the
scenario you want to inspect, then add EventTrace.Record calls at the points in
your game you want to trace.

title: Event Tracer
content:
#

Event Tracer is a Unity tool for understanding what happened in your game and
why. Record events with their data, connect later events to their causes,
inspect call stacks, and save a session to revisit or share.

It works in the Unity Editor and Development Builds. The browser lets you search
and filter events, follow cause-and-effect links, inspect payload snapshots, and
open the code that recorded an event.


Quick start#

Install the package in a Unity 2022.3 or later project. Open Tools → Achieve →
Event Tracer, start a session, and add recording points to your game code:



Call recording methods on Unity's main thread. Passing a recorded event ID as
parentId links a later event to its cause. When recording from a MonoBehaviour,
pass source: this to let the browser select that object.

Enter Play mode and select an event to inspect its data, cause, effects, source
object, and calling code.


Guides#

 * Installation: install from OpenUPM or a Git URL.
 * Using the browser: inspect events, capture stacks, and save or reopen
   sessions.
 * API reference: recording, configuration, snapshots, and capture limits.


Demo#

Import Shop Demo from the package's Samples section in Package Manager, then run
Tools → Achieve → Samples → Create Shop Trace Demo. Enter Play mode and click
Buy FireSword in the Game view. The demo intentionally charges twice, so select
Shop.Purchase in Event Tracer to see its two Wallet.Spend effects.

Use Reset shop / new session in the Game view to start over.
